title: Exponential online mistakes for isotropic Bayesian threshold networks at all sufficiently large widths
status: Conventional proof with independent AI-agent mathematical reviews; not Lean formalized.
review_scope: Three independent final-source reviews checked the arithmetic scaffold, every helper inequality, the exact common-mode ray, whole Gaussian function cones, radial integration and adjacent ratios, the finite-width posterior bound over all Boolean outputs, fixed-gamma quantifiers, the explicit fixed sequence and exact mistake count, bounded teacher and linear Boolean circuit, and IID guarantee. All review records identify both final source hashes. The sole requested change clarified the dependence of the width threshold; no mathematical correction was required.
visual_check: Rendered pages 1, 6, 9, and 12 inspected: author order and exact alphabetical footnote, helper-ray proof, cone ratio and explicit constants, and scope/reference. No clipping or malformed mathematics observed.

author_check.exact_footnote: Authors are listed in alphabetical order.
author_check.pdf_author_metadata: ChatGPT-6 Astra; Kaarel Hanni; Dmitry Vaintrob

critical_scope: Fixed discontinuous sign activation; one hidden layer, constant input, full Boolean cube, exactly isotropic Gaussian coefficients, strict global output margin greater than one half, and exact labels.
For each k>=2, dimension d=167k+1617, target Boolean circuit size Theta(k), width-one teacher with every weight at most one and output margin one.
Calibration prefix has 2^(d-1)+2 examples; there are 2^k-1 surviving finite cutoff functions and exactly 2^k-2 designated mistakes.

For every fixed gamma>1 and every fixed positive variance prefactor, the conclusions hold at every sufficiently large width. Gamma=1 requires a sufficiently small fixed prefactor; unit-prefactor gamma=1 is not covered.
The cold-posterior width threshold is polynomial(k)*2^k with a logarithmic confidence factor. The direct fixed-gamma width threshold has an additional dimension-dependent requirement.
The actual posterior comparison includes every Boolean function, including nonthreshold outputs. It does not restrict the posterior to scalar or threshold subnetworks.
The same target and prior have IID sample bound O((d^2+log(1/beta))/epsilon), at every sufficiently large width.
No result for ordinary tanh, ReLU, GELU, a short calibration prefix, or every width above the teacher width is asserted.
